meta.name: Carrying Out a Test for the Slope (9.5)
meta.subject: AP Statistics
meta.description: Practice computing the slope-test statistic, setting up the p-value, interpreting the p-value, stating a conclusion, and comparing evidence strength for tests about the slope of a regression model.

inputs.label: Which calculation gives the correct test statistic?
Which setup gives the correct p-value?
Which interpretation of the p-value is correct?
Which comparison of evidence strength is correct?

perField.test_statistic_choice: Subtract the null slope first, then divide by the standard error of the slope. For a slope test, use t = (b - beta_0) / SE_b, and in these lesson cases beta_0 = 0.
perField.p_value_setup_choice: Use a t-distribution with df = n - 2, then match the shaded tail area to the alternative hypothesis. One-sided alternatives use one tail; a two-sided alternative uses both tails.
perField.p_value_interpretation_choice: A correct interpretation assumes H0 is true and describes getting evidence this strong or stronger by chance alone. Include the correct tail wording for one-sided vs two-sided.
perField.conclusion_choice: If p-value <= alpha, reject H0. If p-value > alpha, fail to reject H0. The last sentence should describe whether there is convincing statistical evidence for the alternative in context.
perField.strength_comparison_choice: Stronger evidence for a linear relationship comes from a smaller p-value or a t statistic farther from 0.
